messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Elementary Questions on SNA, ERGM and MTML
messages.body_plain:
Dear respected scholars,


Hope you are in great condition.


I?m sorry if my questions look elementary, but studying SNA here in
Malaysia is challenging. We don?t have prominent academician in this area
and the revision need heavily rely on journals and books.

In my situation, I?ve get to know SNA via Multitheoretical Multilevel
(MTML) Model by Professor Monge and Contractor. Through their work and
several other scholars, I have some primary understanding on


i) Testing Hypothesis in Social Network Analysis

ii) Exponential Random Graph Modelling.



So far, in my understanding (which I?m not sure is true or not), We can
test external factors (variables) effect on the network structure. Means
like the factors (such as power, education, and gender) could affect the
outcomes of network structure (the centrality, transitivity, dyad etc.).
And the hypothesis testing is done by using inferential network statistic
such us ERGM. In other word, MTML can be used to predict the antecedents of
network structure.

Thus my first question is


*?Is the above statement is true? And does the hypothesis testing can only
be done by using ERGM?*?


Then, come the confusing part. I try to browse articles on SNA, ERGM etc.
to understand whether we can use network statistical analysis to measure
the impact of network structure on dependent variable. For instance, By
using ERGM we can measure the impact of network structure on consumer
loyalty or on brand reputation. However, through my searching process, I
could not identify or prove that the statement is correct.


Thus the second question is


*?Can we measure the impact of network structure (the whole graph) on
external dependent variable (e.g. corporate image, innovation acceptance
etc.)? Through network statistical analysis??*


To conclude this, I just want to share my aspiration on embarking social
network analysis as an area to explore for my doctoral study. The
aspiration is because I would like to understand the power of network on
affecting corporate image. Plus, I would also like to cultivate the study
on SNA especially the inferential aspect in Malaysia.

Again, I apologize if the questions look elementary but I do need
reassurance on my thought. If not, I would just blindly explore this area.
A thing that I always afraid in research. Thanks for the help



Regards,

Ammar Redza

Malaysia

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Multilevel ergm in Statnet?
messages.body_plain:
This is only possible if PNet has a publicly documented API. At the very 
least, they must declare their classes as public in order for you to use 
them with rJava. PNet, however, does not seem to have classes declared 
as public, at least I can't see any because the source code is not 
available (at least not on http://sna.unimelb.edu.au/PNet). What is 
more, the version needed for fitting multilevel ERGMs, MPNet, is only 
available as an EXE file, and rJava requires a .jar or .class file.

Unless they make their source code available or provide an API, the more 
promising avenue is to write a wrapper for the functions contained in 
the ergm package (e.g., ergm.Cprepare, ergm.design etc., or just ergm) 
that takes multiple dependent networks, combines them in a 
block-diagonal matrix using the bdiag function in the Matrix package (I 
think there are even facilities for fitting block-diagonal models in the 
ergm package), creates a matrix that specifies which dyad belongs to 
which network (as input information for the multi-level model terms) and 
fits an ergm with some new user terms where the user can specify the 
interactions between the "dependent" networks (e.g., a triadic closure 
term with a twopath ijk in one network and the closure ik of that triad 
in the other network; or a GWESP term that returns different counts for 
the different blocks of the matrix). I *think* something like this could 
fully rely on the MCMC code and package infrastructure that is already 
there, so it shouldn't be too big of a project (except for coding the 
statistics). I would do it if I had time.

Another helpful thing would be a dictionary that translates terms 
between statnet, PNet, and SIENA. I hope others will feel encouraged to 
come up with something like this at some point.

Take care,

Philip

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Katherine.  Such models should probably be viewed as "multi-mode" 
networks, rather than "multi-level" networks, but the terminology in the 
field is hopelessly muddled at this point.  These can be fit within 
ergm(), but you will need:

1. To ensure that you have set any constraints necessary to prevent ties 
among entities that cannot in theory be tied; and

2. To employ a set of statistics that implement the inhomogeneities 
inherent in the model class you seek.  As others have noted, this may 
require you to implement your own statistics using the ergm userterms 
package, but it can be done (and once those terms are implemented, they 
will interoperate with the rest of the statnet suite).

Hope that helps,

-Carter

messages.body_plain:
Dear Jeff,

On Fri, 2015-04-17 at 01:59 +1000, Jeffrey Alan Carnegie wrote: 

> I need to get an example of STREGM using edgecov or dyadcov as terms
> for a directed network outcome. When I run the code below, I am
> getting an error, which Nicole says has to do with NAs in a matrix
> which gets blown up to 36x36 instead of 18x18. She can get it to work
> by increasing the size of the matrix attribute, but I am not sure what
> the other 18 rows and columns mean.


This is a bug in tergm. The "blown up" thing is supposed to happen, as
the current implementation of stergm CMLE works by constructing a pair
of block-diagonal networks with the following sociomatrices:


[y0  0]
[ 0 y1]

[y1  0]
[ 0 y2]


and fitting the transition from the first block-diagonal network to the
second (and thus from y0 to y1 and from y1 to y2). When it combines the
networks in this way, it tries to guess when you have a dyadic
covariate, by looking to see if there are any network attributes that
are matrices of appropriate dimension, and, if so, constructing a
block-diagonal matrix out of them. Unfortunately, I I've put NAs in
place of the structural zeros, forgetting that R's C calling routines
are allergic to those.

We'll fix it in the next release, but, for now, if you can rebuild tergm
from source, you can fix it as follows:

     1. In tergm source's R directory, open combine.networks.R.
     2. Find the line containing "m <- matrix(NA, sum(ns), sum(ns))". It
        should be Line 42, or close.
     3. In that line, replace "NA" with "0", save, rebuild, and
        reinstall.


Note that this workaround may fail if you have a non-numeric covariate
matrix. If you can't rebuild, I can try to send a patched build to you
in the next day or two.

                            Best,
                            Pavel

P.S. The reason Nicole's trick works is that if the attribute matrix is
no longer n*n, the code that tries to detect dyadic covariates no longer
treats it as such and leaves it alone.

--

Hi Joe -

R 3.2.0 was released just last week.  Any time a new major R release 
happens, all of the contributed packages need to be rebuilt by the CRAN 
team for it.  My understanding is that this is all done by volunteers, 
and there is a larger pool of volunteers for the Windows builds than for 
the MacOS builds.  Consequently, it can take some time (up to a week or 
so?) after a major R release for all of the packages to be available 
again in pre-built forms for Mac.  (I may have some of the details 
wrong, but I think I'm capturing the big picture).

This means your options are:

(1) Wait a few days
(2) Build the packages you want from source - instructions abound online
(3) Switch to a Windows machine for the time being
(4) Revert to R 3.1.X

HTH,
Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ergm: non-integer "receiver" target.stats
messages.body_plain:
Hi Carlo,

Unfortunately, receiver stats are not "ensembles" -- they are node 
specific integer counts of ties.  If you combine other nodes into the 
base, it can function as an ensemble for a target count.  So, if you put 5 
nodes into the base, and have a target of 1 tie, each node would get your 
0.2 ties in expectation.  Alternatively, you might be able to set the coef 
for this receiver node using an offset to achieve the desired tie 
probability, but the value may be difficult to find given the correlation 
with other terms in the model.

I'm replying to the list here in case someone else has a better idea.

best,
mm
